claim_one_line: THIRD ADDENDUM -- ONE-CUSPED ISOTROPY BROADENED AND NOT BROKEN. B1334's addendum leaves isotropy as the ONLY live route for the one-cusped case, so it was attacked: six further one-cusped manifolds (m003, m006, m009, m035, m039, m040), GEOMETRIC holonomy, CHARACTERISTIC ZERO at 40 digits, germ sums included -- 106 sectors of which 84 NON-VACUOUS, imposing 128 genuine scalar equations, ALL ISOTROPIC, zero non-isotropic, zero inconclusive. Eighteen are odd-parity, where the invariant form is alternating and the induced pairing symmetric, so <x,x> = 0 is a real equation even at dim L = 1. Two errors were caught en route and are recorded: a first pass using only single germs returned 48 sectors that were ALL VACUOUS (a single Sym^m gives t_0 = 1 with even m) and would have read as 48 isotropic, caught by the vacuity accounting this arc added after its own section 2; and with sums added, 19 sectors read NOT ISOTROPIC, every one the mixed germ Sym^2 (+) Sym^4, an artifact of testing against EVERY pi_1(T)-invariant form when the duality uses only the SL2-invariant ones -- exactly the cross-term distinction section 3 had already drawn -- and against the correct forms all 19 are isotropic, the 1e-7 to 1e-5 relative magnitudes having been a tell that the thresholds now treat as INCONCLUSIVE rather than as a finding. So one-cusped isotropy now rests on 128 genuine scalar equations across NINE manifolds with an explicit vacuity audit. It did not break; it remains unproved; it remains the only live route. SECOND CORRECTION: section 1's reduction is stated too strongly. Isotropy of L_V ALONE gives only dim L_V <= t_1/2, not equality; equality needs L_{V*} isotropic too, which does not follow. B1335's m010 sector over F_13 is an explicit counterexample -- L_V = 0 is isotropic for all four of its invariant forms, t_1/2 = 1, and yet I = t_0 - r_1 = 1, consistency being restored by L_{V*} having dimension 2 > t_1/2 and so failing isotropy (Gram [[0,3],[3,0]], symmetric as the odd-m parity requires). As a statement about the whole CLASS the reduction is sound, since V* lies in the class too, and 'prove isotropy for the class' remains the right target for the one-cusped case. No computed result changes: every one-cusped sector here has BOTH L_V and L_V* isotropic. SCOPE CORRECTION FIRST (B1333 addendum, next day): EVERYTHING IN THIS ARC IS A ONE-CUSP STATEMENT. With several cusps L_V is usually NOT isotropic and L_V != L_V* -- 36 of 40 sectors across 14 chiral multi-cusped covers of m004 -- and the index vanishes anyway in all 40, so the implication isotropy => I = 0 stands but the REDUCTION IS NOT AN EQUIVALENCE: isotropy is sufficient, not necessary, and proving it settles the one-cusped case only. With that scope: THE VANISHING IS A FORM-FREE CUP-PRODUCT STATEMENT, AND CUSP-TRIVIALITY IS WHAT MAKES IT LEGAL. First, why the question exists at all: V = Sym^m (x) psi with psi of order 3 admits NO invariant bilinear form (that needs psi^2 = 1), so B1329 was right that isotropy fails globally and 'isotropic' has no referent upstairs. But the domain D FORCES psi cusp-trivial, hence V|_T = Sym^m = V*|_T as the SAME pi_1(T)-module, which is STRICTLY STRONGER than the t_0 = t_0* that B1297's domain D already STATES as part of its own definition (so t_0 = t_1/2 was never news, and t_1 = 2 t_0 shows in every computed sector as it must): equal dimensions would not put L_V and L_V* in one space, the SAME MODULE does, and that is the upgrade from a domain condition to a well-posed isotropy question. Cusp-locality is therefore not a candidate MECHANISM as B1331 guessed, it is the precondition for the QUESTION. Second, the evidence, exactly over Q(zeta_12) on the geometric holonomy of three CHIRAL targets s958, t12833, t12835: 18 sectors each, I = 0 and L_V = L_V* and r_1 = t_0 = t_1/2 in all 54, zero exceptions -- BUT six sectors per manifold are VACUOUS, because for even m the induced pairing is alternating and every 1-dimensional subspace is isotropic for free; only the 12 sectors with dim L_V >= 2 carry content, 18 genuine scalar equations per manifold. Third, the sharpening that repairs this: L_V is isotropic for EVERY pi_1(T)-invariant form (12/12, 20/20, 27/27 by dimension, isotropy being linear in the form), and invariant forms are exactly the functionals on H^2(T;W (x) W) = (W (x) W)_{pi_1 T}, so the statement can be made FORM-FREE and verified directly as a class. It must be stated carefully: for germs with irreducible or isomorphic summands the class vanishes outright (cup classes span dimension 0 inside an H^2 of dimension 3, 5 and 12 for Sym^2, Sym^4 and Sym^2 (+) Sym^2), which is NON-VACUOUS precisely in the dim L_V = 1 sectors the form-based test could not speak to; but for Sym^2 (+) Sym^4, whose summands are NON-ISOMORPHIC, the class is NONZERO, spanning dimension 2 in a 14-dimensional H^2 -- so the blanket claim 'L_V u L_V = 0' would be FALSE. Block-decomposing W (x) W settles it: the surviving dimension 2 lies ENTIRELY in the off-diagonal blocks Sym^a (x) Sym^b with a != b, while the DIAGONAL blocks vanish. Since Hom_{SL2}(Sym^a,(Sym^b)^*) = 0 for a != b, the off-diagonal part carries no invariant functional at all and is invisible to every form and hence to every duality statement -- which is also exactly why the Sym^2 (+) Sym^4 form count reads 12 of 14 rather than 14 of 14. The correct statement is therefore: L_V u L_V vanishes in every component of H^2(T;W (x) W) carrying an SL2-invariant functional, which for irreducible W is the whole class. This implies I = 0 for every choice of duality at once and is what should be proved. Galois stays ruled out: all three targets are chiral. The cup product implementation was validated first and independently -- coboundaries annihilate every cocycle, the invariant form is SOLVED for rather than quoted (one per Sym^m, alternating for m odd and symmetric for m even, full rank), and the Gram on H^1(T;W) is perfect -- on four commuting families, m = 1..6.
